title: 01. Fundamentals: 14. Strings, Bytes, Encoding & Regex
summary: Master text, binary data, formatting, Unicode, and the re module.

sections.title: 1. str — Immutable Unicode Sequences
sections.body:
> Master text, binary data, formatting, Unicode, and the `re` module.

A `str` is an immutable sequence of Unicode code points. Every modification creates a new object.

```python
s = "café"
len(s)           # 4 — code points, not bytes
s[0]             # 'c'
s + "!"          # new string
s.replace("é", "e")   # new string
```

CPython uses **PEP 393 flexible representation**: depending on the highest code point, a string is stored as 1, 2, or 4 bytes per character internally. Indexing is O(1).

diagrams.title: Why "".join() beats += in a loop
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  subgraph P["s += piece in a loop"]
    s1["'a'"] --> s2["new 'ab'"] --> s3["new 'abc'"] --> s4["new 'abcd' … each step copies everything"]
  end
  subgraph J["''.join(pieces)"]
    parts["['a','b','c','d']"] --> one["measure total size once, copy once → 'abcd'"]
  end
diagrams.explain: Strings are immutable, so `+=` builds a brand-new string each time and copies all previous characters — quadratic work in a loop. `''.join(list)` computes the final size once and copies each piece once. (CPython sometimes optimises `+=` in place, but do not rely on it.)

sections.title: 2. Building Strings Efficiently
sections.body:
`+=` in a loop is O(n²) (each step copies). Use `"".join(parts)`:

```python
# Bad
out = ""
for x in items: out += str(x)

# Good
out = "".join(str(x) for x in items)
```

For lots of fragments, build a list and join once.

sections.title: 3. Essential str Methods
sections.body:
### Case

| Method                                  | Notes                                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `upper()`, `lower()`                    | locale-independent                                             |
| `casefold()`                            | aggressive lowercase for case-insensitive compare (`ß` → `ss`) |
| `title()`, `capitalize()`, `swapcase()` |                                                                |

### Test (return bool)

`isalpha`, `isdigit`, `isnumeric`, `isdecimal`, `isalnum`, `isspace`, `isupper`, `islower`, `isidentifier`, `isascii`, `isprintable`, `startswith`, `endswith` (last two accept tuple).

### Search

| Method        | Returns               |
| ------------- | --------------------- |
| `find(sub)`   | index or `-1`         |
| `rfind(sub)`  | from right            |
| `index(sub)`  | index or `ValueError` |
| `count(sub)`  | int                   |
| `in` operator | bool                  |

### Split / Join

```python
"a,b,c".split(",")          # ['a','b','c']
"a,b,c".split(",", 1)       # ['a', 'b,c']
"a,b,c".rsplit(",", 1)      # ['a,b', 'c']
"a\nb\nc".splitlines()      # ['a','b','c']  — handles \r\n, \r too
"a b   c".split()           # ['a','b','c']  — runs of whitespace
",".join(["a","b","c"])     # 'a,b,c'
```

### Strip

```python
"  hi  ".strip()            # 'hi'
"--hi--".strip("-")         # 'hi'   (set of chars to remove, NOT a substring)
"abcXYZ".removeprefix("abc")   # 3.9+ → 'XYZ'
"abcXYZ".removesuffix("XYZ")   # 3.9+ → 'abc'
```

> ⚠️ `"hello".strip("hi")` → `"ello"`, not `"ello"` — `strip` treats arg as a _character set_. Use `removeprefix`/`removesuffix` for substring trim.

### Replace

```python
"a.b.c".replace(".", "/")        # 'a/b/c'
"a.b.c".replace(".", "/", 1)     # 'a/b.c'
```

### Translate

Fastest way to apply a character mapping:

```python
table = str.maketrans({"a": "1", "b": "2"})
"ab".translate(table)              # '12'
del_table = str.maketrans("", "", "aeiou")
"hello".translate(del_table)       # 'hll'
```

sections.title: 4. Formatting — Four Eras
sections.body:
### 4.1 `%` (oldest, C-style)

```python
"Hello %s, you are %d" % ("Ana", 30)
```

### 4.2 `str.format`

```python
"Hello {}, age {}".format("Ana", 30)
"{name} is {age}".format(name="Ana", age=30)
"{0} {0}".format("hi")   # positional reuse
```

### 4.3 f-strings (PEP 498) — preferred

```python
name = "Ana"; age = 30
f"Hello {name}, age {age}"
f"{name=}"                 # 3.8+ → "name='Ana'"  (debug)
f"{age:>5}"                # right-align width 5
f"{3.14159:.2f}"           # '3.14'
f"{1_000_000:,}"           # '1,000,000'
f"{0xff:#06x}"             # '0x00ff'
f"{value!r}"               # repr conversion
```

Format spec: `[[fill]align][sign][#][0][width][,][.precision][type]`
| Type | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `d`, `b`, `o`, `x`, `X` | int formats |
| `f`, `e`, `g`, `%` | float formats |
| `s` | string |
| `c` | char from int |

PEP 701 (3.12) lifted nesting/quote restrictions:

```python
# 3.12+
f"{ {1,2,3} }"       # set literal inside
f"{"a" + "b"}"       # nested quotes OK
```

### 4.4 `Template` (safer for user-supplied strings)

```python
from string import Template
Template("Hello $name").substitute(name="Ana")
```

### Comparison

|           | Speed   | Readability | Use when                |
| --------- | ------- | ----------- | ----------------------- |
| f-string  | fastest | best        | almost always           |
| `.format` | fast    | good        | dynamic format strings  |
| `%`       | fast    | dated       | logging-style legacy    |
| Template  | slowest | safe        | user-supplied templates |

sections.title: 5. bytes and bytearray
sections.body:
| Type         | Mutable                    | Literal              |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `bytes`      | no                         | `b"abc"`             |
| `bytearray`  | yes                        | `bytearray(b"abc")`  |
| `memoryview` | views into bytes/bytearray | `memoryview(b"abc")` |

```python
b = b"hello"            # bytes — immutable
b[0]                    # 104  (an int!)
b[0:1]                  # b'h'
list(b)                 # [104, 101, 108, 108, 111]

ba = bytearray(b"hi")
ba[0] = 72              # mutate
ba                      # bytearray(b'Hi')
```

`bytes` does **not** auto-decode in comparisons:

```python
b"abc" == "abc"   # False
```

sections.title: 6. Encoding / Decoding
sections.body:
`str` ↔ `bytes` always requires an encoding (default `utf-8`).

```python
s = "café"
b = s.encode("utf-8")          # b'caf\xc3\xa9'
b.decode("utf-8")              # 'café'

s.encode("ascii")              # UnicodeEncodeError
s.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")    # b'caf'
s.encode("ascii", errors="replace")   # b'caf?'
s.encode("ascii", errors="backslashreplace")  # b'caf\\xe9'
```

| `errors=`           | Behavior                           |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `strict` (default)  | raise                              |
| `ignore`            | drop offending                     |
| `replace`           | `?` (encode) / `U+FFFD` (decode)   |
| `backslashreplace`  | `\xNN` literal                     |
| `surrogateescape`   | preserve invalid bytes (filenames) |
| `xmlcharrefreplace` | `&#NNN;` (encode-only)             |

**Always specify `encoding=` when opening text files** — defaults differ between platforms.

sections.title: 7. Unicode Normalization
sections.body:
Some characters have multiple representations (`é` = `U+00E9` **or** `e + U+0301`). Compare equality only after normalizing.

```python
import unicodedata
a = "café"; b = "cafe\u0301"
a == b                                   # False!
unicodedata.normalize("NFC", a) == unicodedata.normalize("NFC", b)   # True
```

Forms:

- **NFC**: composed (default for most data)
- **NFD**: decomposed (base + combining marks)
- **NFKC**, **NFKD**: compatibility (also unifies `①` → `1`, ligatures, half-width)

For _case-insensitive_ comparison, combine with `casefold`:

```python
def streq(a, b):
    n = lambda s: unicodedata.normalize("NFC", s).casefold()
    return n(a) == n(b)
```

sections.title: 8. The re Module — Regular Expressions
sections.body:
### Core functions

| Function              | Use                               |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `re.match(p, s)`      | match at start only               |
| `re.search(p, s)`     | first match anywhere              |
| `re.fullmatch(p, s)`  | entire string                     |
| `re.findall(p, s)`    | list of strings/tuples            |
| `re.finditer(p, s)`   | iterator of `Match` objects       |
| `re.sub(p, repl, s)`  | replace; `repl` can be a function |
| `re.subn(p, repl, s)` | (new_str, count)                  |
| `re.split(p, s)`      | split on pattern                  |
| `re.compile(p)`       | reusable Pattern                  |

### Compile for reuse

```python
import re
pat = re.compile(r"\b(\d{3})-(\d{4})\b")
for m in pat.finditer(text):
    area, num = m.group(1), m.group(2)
```

### Match object API

```python
m.group(0)      # whole match
m.group(1)      # first group
m.groups()      # tuple of all groups
m.groupdict()   # named groups dict
m.start(); m.end(); m.span()
```

### Flags

| Flag   | Inline | Effect                                         |
| ------ | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `re.I` | `(?i)` | case-insensitive                               |
| `re.M` | `(?m)` | `^`/`$` match line edges                       |
| `re.S` | `(?s)` | `.` matches newline                            |
| `re.X` | `(?x)` | verbose: ignore whitespace, allow `#` comments |
| `re.A` | `(?a)` | ASCII-only `\w`, `\d`, `\s`                    |
| `re.U` | `(?u)` | Unicode (default in 3)                         |

### Groups

```python
r"(?P<area>\d{3})-(?P<num>\d{4})"     # named groups
r"(?:abc)"                             # non-capturing group
r"(\d+)\1"                             # backreference \1
r"(?P=area)"                           # backreference to named group
```

### Lookarounds (zero-width)

```python
r"(?=foo)"        # lookahead positive
r"(?!foo)"        # lookahead negative
r"(?<=foo)"       # lookbehind positive (fixed width)
r"(?<!foo)"       # lookbehind negative
```

### `sub` with function

```python
re.sub(r"\d+", lambda m: str(int(m.group()) * 2), "a1 b2 c3")
# 'a2 b4 c6'
```

### Verbose pattern

```python
pat = re.compile(r"""
    \b
    (\d{3})        # area code
    -
    (\d{4})        # number
    \b
""", re.X)
```

### Performance tips

- **Compile** once if used repeatedly.
- Avoid catastrophic backtracking: nested quantifiers like `(a+)+` on near-matches blow up. Use atomic groups (3.11+: `(?>...)`) or possessive quantifiers, or simplify pattern.
- For simple substring search, `in` and `str.find` are far faster than regex.
- For large alternation, consider `re.compile("|".join(map(re.escape, words)))` and let the engine build a trie internally — or use the `regex` PyPI module / Aho-Corasick for very large dictionaries.

### `re.escape`

Escape user input before injecting into a pattern:

```python
re.search(re.escape(user_input), text)
```

sections.title: 9. Common String / Regex Patterns
sections.body:
```python
# Email-ish (simplified — never use a "perfect" email regex)
re.fullmatch(r"[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+", s)

# Slugify
re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "-", s.lower()).strip("-")

# Whitespace collapse
re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()

# Extract numbers
list(map(int, re.findall(r"-?\d+", s)))

# Replace ${VAR} placeholders
re.sub(r"\$\{(\w+)\}", lambda m: env[m.group(1)], template)
```

sections.title: 10. Anti-Patterns
sections.body:
| Bad                                    | Why                       | Better                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Parse HTML/JSON with regex             | broken in subtle ways     | Use a parser (`lxml`, `json`)     |
| Concatenate in a loop                  | O(n²)                     | `"".join(parts)`                  |
| `open(path)` (no encoding)             | platform-dependent        | `open(path, encoding="utf-8")`    |
| Compare bytes/str without encoding     | always False              | `.decode()` first                 |
| Use `.strip("foo")` for prefix removal | strips chars in any order | `removeprefix("foo")`             |
| Hand-rolled email/URL regex            | always wrong              | `email-validator`, `urllib.parse` |
